domain: Operations, infrastructure, and the agent fleet (agents/, scripts/ reporting pipeline, machine fleet M1-M4, PG bus, CI)
one_line: A 43-agent paper fleet with exactly two live daemons (both on M4), a live-but-silent Postgres backbone on M1, two cold GPU boxes, and a zombie reporting loop that has been emailing a frozen 2026-06-24 snapshot 5-6x/day for seven weeks because PgRedis lacks a 10-line `exists()` method.
purpose_and_thesis: Provide the operational fabric for a multi-machine autonomous research fleet: Agora heartbeats/message bus for cross-agent coordination, a Pronoia-orchestrated reporting pipeline (portfolio_monitor -> Metis LLM brief -> git auto-commit -> daily email) so James has continuous operational awareness, machine probes for hardware telemetry, and CI-side capability tracking of the math arsenal. Founding design: pivot/agent_portfolio_and_monitoring_2026-05-12.md (cited at scripts/portfolio_monitor.py:14); bus originally Redis on M1, migrated to Postgres 2026-06-24 after James: "Redis is too difficult to keep running under WSL" (roles/Ergon/REDIS_TO_POSTGRES_2026-06-24.md).

FLEET MASS-DEATH: every M1/M2/M3 heartbeat stops within 45 minutes (agora.agent_heartbeats: Hephaestus 12:24:52, Charon_Loop 12:24:54, Pythia 12:24:42, all M2 swarm 11:55-12:24). research_queue last dispatch same morning 06:16. Only M4 survived. Cause not established in surveyed docs.

Outage finally noticed — 24 days later — via M4 monitor email ('fleet 0/43 down'). Aporia writes INFRA_RECOVERY_PLAN. M3/GANDALF found hardware-dead (mobo+CPU). Verified M1 IP had silently moved .176 -> .202; all configs were dialing a dead host.

SAME DAY: portfolio_monitor begins crashing every cycle ('PgRedis' object has no attribute 'exists') — docs/state.json freezes forever at 2026-06-24T12:15:10Z.

Zombie era: intelligence_loop keeps running on M4, regenerating the LLM brief from the frozen snapshot every 4h — 442 'auto: portfolio update' commits total, each touching only docs/portfolio_brief.md; 59 stale-alert emails dispatched in August alone. All other daemons silent.

strategic_read: The operational truth is stark: this is not a degraded fleet, it is a dead fleet with a live database and a live liar. Since 2026-06-24 the program's only continuous activity has been (a) M4 re-narrating a frozen snapshot via LLM 6x/day — burning tokens to produce provably false operational claims that get emailed to the human decision-maker — and (b) a cloud cron noting numpy version bumps. Meanwhile the genuinely valuable substrate (M1 Postgres: 363GB LMFDB, migrated kill/sigma/charon schemas, 422 finished research reports) is up, reachable, and consumed by nothing. Three implications. First, ops debt is trivially small relative to its distortion: one ~10-line PgRedis patch (exists/zcard/hlen) makes telemetry truthful again, and one decision (stop or fix intelligence_loop) stops the misinformation channel; do these before any strategy discussion, because current dashboards will corrupt any assessment that trusts them. Second, the 43-agent daemon architecture is empirically falsified as an operating model for a one-human program: it died in 45 minutes, went unnoticed for 24 days, and its revival never happened even after every blocker (hardware, Redis, config) was cleared — the live pattern that actually works is what happened today: human-driven Claude sessions (Techne, Ergon) coordinating through committed role files and a shared Postgres. The program should formally retire the daemon monoculture (the lifecycle fields already exist in EXPECTED_AGENTS) and design around session-driven work + a handful of cheap, self-healing cron jobs with watchdogs. Third, compute allocation is inverted: the only live box has the weakest GPU (Quadro P500) while two RTX 5060 Ti machines and the forge box sit dark — if the M1-metabolization experiment is still the decider, the ops prerequisite is not a fleet revival, it is powering one GPU box and pointing one session at it. Commit roles/Hephaestus/ to git today; it is the decider's charter and it exists on exactly one disk.
